summary: Candidate A is substantially closer to the frozen contract: its Files.Upload uses the established multipart helper and delegates to Files.Add. Candidate B has stronger tests and documentation, but violates two central constraints by duplicating Files.Add logic and changing global request/retry machinery.
reasons: A implements the required signature, uses multipartbody.NewFile("file", fileName, content), and routes the result through s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), preserving established option, request, decoding, and error behavior.
B reimplements Files.Add inside Upload by constructing options, invoking Raw.Do, and decoding the response itself, directly violating the requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add.
B changes RawClient.Do to buffer arbitrary reader bodies across the SDK. This is explicitly outside scope and changes memory, reader-consumption, and error timing semantics for existing APIs.

B's tests are materially more complete: they verify field name, filename, content, options, validation, source-reader errors, and retry behavior. A's tests omit content verification, validation cases, and source-reader failure coverage required by the contract.
risks_a: A adds the unrelated public PersonsService.UploadPicture API and tests, violating scope discipline and the instruction to add exactly the specified convenience API.
The exported Upload method lacks a Go documentation comment.
Its multipart test opens the file part but never verifies its content, and required validation/source-reader error tests are missing.
risks_b: Upload duplicates Files.Add machinery instead of delegating to it, creating maintenance and behavioral-drift risk.

The global replayableReader change broadens buffering to all opaque io.Reader request bodies unless WithNoRetry is explicitly present, even beyond file uploads and regardless of whether retry policy will actually retry the request.
It changes existing Files.Add and Files.Update behavior despite the contract requiring Add's existing behavior to be preserved and unrelated retry machinery to remain untouched.
